HeadUndoReason.description:
Why HEAD cannot be undone (`git.status.headUndoReason`). `detached`, `root`, `merge` and `pushed` are the
`reason` that `git.undoCommit` answers with `undo-unavailable`.

oneOf.description: HEAD is detached: there is no branch whose last commit could be undone.
The last commit is the repository's first, or there is no commit.
The last commit is a merge.
A remote branch contains the last commit: undoing it would need a force push.
The companion's git could not tell (`git.undoCommit` answers `internal`).

diskBytesHash.description:
For a regular file that has no `diskHash` (binary, or above the text limit): SHA-256 (hex) of its bytes, so
that a commit or rollback can tell it changed since it was shown. Null otherwise.

diskHash.description:
The version of the file on disk: SHA-256 (hex) of its text as `file.read` returns it (decoded, without a
byte order mark, `\n` line ends) — the same hash as `file.read.hash` and `git.hunks.diskHash`. Null when
the file is deleted, not a regular file, binary or above the text limit.

stagedOutside.description: The index holds a version of this file other than HEAD's (staged from a terminal).

headUndoReason.description: Why not, when `headUndoable` is false; null when it is true.

headUndoable.description:
Whether `git.undoCommit` would undo HEAD now: the same check it makes (a writable project, a branch, a
commit with one parent that no remote branch contains). The page may still get `undo-unavailable` when HEAD
moves before it asks, and `rate-limited` while another git operation runs.

summary: Changed and unversioned files, grouped as in a commit window; whether HEAD can be undone.
